Fit a G2G Model with Time-Invariant Covariates

Source: R/G2G_static_functions.R
G2G_static_MLE.Rd

Fits a Grassia(II)-Geometric (G2G) survival model with time-invariant covariates using maximum likelihood estimation via BFGS. Each subject is represented by a single row. The survivor function at discrete period \(t\) is \(S(t) = (1 + t \cdot \exp(\mathbf{x}'\boldsymbol{\beta}) / \alpha)^{-r}\), where \(r\) and \(\alpha\) are the shape and rate of the Gamma mixing distribution and \(\boldsymbol{\beta}\) are covariate log-hazard coefficients.

Covariates are centered and scaled internally to keep the likelihood numerically stable, and the results are converted back to the original covariate scale.

Usage

G2G_static_MLE(formula, data, level = 0.95)

Arguments

formula

A formula of the form Surv(time, status) ~ x1 + x2 + ... where time is the observed period, status is the event indicator (1 = event, 0 = censored), and x1, x2, etc. are time-invariant covariates. Transformations, interactions and factors are allowed on the right-hand side, but the intercept must be kept (no - 1 or + 0): the intercept column is always dropped, because \(\alpha\) plays its role.

data

A data frame containing all variables referenced in formula. One row per subject. The observed times must be whole numbers >= 1 (discrete periods).

level

Confidence level for the Wald confidence intervals, a single number strictly between 0 and 1. Default is 0.95.

Value

A list of class "G2Gcov" containing the optimization results from optim with the following additional elements. All estimates, standard errors and confidence bounds are reported on the original covariate scale (only hessian is on the internal parameterization):

par

Named numeric vector of parameter estimates. The first two elements are r (shape) and alpha (rate), returned on the natural (exponentiated) scale. Remaining elements are covariate log-hazard coefficients in original units.

par_stderr

Standard errors on the original scale (named like par). For r and alpha these come from the delta method (e.g. SE(r) is approximately r * SE(log r)). If the Hessian at the optimum is not positive definite (or cannot be inverted) a warning is issued and these are NA.

par_upper

Upper bounds of the Wald confidence intervals at the requested level. For r and alpha the interval is formed on the log scale and exponentiated.

par_lower

Lower bounds of the Wald confidence intervals at the requested level.

level

The confidence level used for par_lower and par_upper.

value

Negative log-likelihood at the optimum.

convergence

Convergence code from optim (0 = success; a warning is issued for any other code).

hessian

Observed Hessian matrix at the optimum, on the internal parameterization (log r, log alpha, standardized coefficients), with row and column names.

center

Covariate means used internally for centering.

scale

Covariate standard deviations used internally for scaling.

terms

The terms object for the covariates (response removed), used to code new data in G2G_static_survival.

xlevels

Factor levels of the covariates at fitting time, also used to code new data.

See also

G2G_varying_MLE for the time-varying extension; G2G_static_survival and G2G_static_retention for the fitted curves; plot_p0 to visualize the fitted baseline propensity distribution.

Examples

# \donttest{
  if (requireNamespace("survival", quietly = TRUE)) {
    library(survival)
    fit <- G2G_static_MLE(Surv(time, status) ~ age + karno, data = veteran)
    print(fit)

    # 90% confidence intervals instead of the default 95%
    fit90 <- G2G_static_MLE(
      Surv(time, status) ~ age + karno,
      data  = veteran,
      level = 0.90
    )
  }
#> G2G Model Fit
#> ---------------------------------------------------- 
#> Convergence:       Converged (code 0)
#> Log-likelihood:    -723.3544
#> AIC:               1454.7087
#> Parameters:        4
#> 
#> Coefficients:
#>              Estimate Std.Error Lower.95 Upper.95
#> r (shape)      5.4654    3.2150   1.7254  17.3117
#> alpha (rate)  48.0151   52.4109   5.6526 407.8554
#> age           -0.0027    0.0102  -0.0228   0.0174
#> karno         -0.0373    0.0054  -0.0478  -0.0267
# }
